date_note: Kyoei Steel announced it on 25 November; the page gives no earlier day for the announcement (unauthorized access was detected on 17 November Japan time).
geo_basis: victim city stated (El Paso, Texas plant of the US subsidiary)
title: Kyoei Steel says its US subsidiary was hit by a cyberattack; no information leak confirmed so far
summary: Nikkei reports that Kyoei Steel announced on 25 November that its US subsidiary, named in the article as ビントン・スチール, with a plant in El Paso, Texas, suffered a cyberattack. The company says unauthorized access was detected on the 17th Japan time and damage spread on the 18th and 19th. It says no leak has been confirmed so far and no direct effect on shipments or plant operations.
plain: Kyoei Steel says its US subsidiary was hit by a cyberattack. The company says no information leak has been confirmed so far and shipments and plant operations are not directly affected.
exec: A Japanese steelmaker says a US subsidiary's networks were attacked; it reports no confirmed leak and no direct effect on shipments or operations.

sources.name: Nikkei: 共英製鋼米子会社にサイバー攻撃 情報漏洩は「現時点で確認されず」
Cybersecurity.com (Japan): 共英製鋼の米国子会社ビントン・スチールがサイバー攻撃を受け社内ネットワークに障害

validation.note: Nikkei and Cybersecurity.com (Japan) are independent publishers that both state the cyberattack on the US subsidiary and no confirmed leak; the company's own disclosure was not read.

review.note: Compared Nikkei and Cybersecurity.com (Japan): subsidiary, 17th detection, 18-19 spread, no leak confirmed, no direct operations impact
